The total line now starts with `TOTAL` at the very start, with no leading spaces. The test run after this change shows 4 passed (exit code 0).

The sum is right-aligned to two decimals in the same 10-wide amount column as the expense lines. The total line is 46 characters wide, the same as an expense line, so the last digits line up. The new test checks that width as well as the exact text. An empty month gives `TOTAL` followed by `0.00` in the same column. The tests check the exact layout I wrote, so they don't prove it looks right on a real report. I haven't run it on a real month's CSV or looked at printed output. Please check one real report. A very long item name or a total over 9,999,999.99 would push the columns out of line.

I changed only `expenses.py` and `tests/test_expenses.py`, the two files you approved. I recorded a decision note for this change. The earlier note that said the label sits under the item column is now out of date, because `TOTAL` is at the start of the line.
row.diff:
diff --git a/expenses.py b/expenses.py
index 064b101..b57a78f 100644
--- a/expenses.py
+++ b/expenses.py
@@ -11,8 +11,12 @@ def read_expenses(path):
 
 
 def report_lines(expenses):
-    """Plain-text lines for the report, one per expense."""
+    """Plain-text lines for the report, one per expense, then a total."""
     lines = []
+    total = 0.0
     for e in expenses:
         lines.append(f"{e['date']}  {e['item']:<24}{e['amount']:>10.2f}")
+        total += e["amount"]
+    # 36 = date (10) + 2 spaces + item (24), so the sum lines up with the amounts.
+    lines.append(f"{'TOTAL':<36}{total:>10.2f}")
     return lines
diff --git a/tests/test_expenses.py b/tests/test_expenses.py
index 3938969..dfed09a 100644
--- a/tests/test_expenses.py
+++ b/tests/test_expenses.py
@@ -7,6 +7,22 @@ def test_expense_line_layout():
     assert lines[0] == "2024-05-03  Price labels" + " " * 12 + "     12.50"
 
 
+def test_report_ends_with_total():
+    lines = expenses.report_lines([
+        {"date": "2024-05-03", "item": "Price labels", "amount": 12.5},
+        {"date": "2024-05-04", "item": "Tape", "amount": 3.2},
+    ])
+    assert len(lines) == 3
+    assert lines[-1].startswith("TOTAL")
+    assert lines[-1] == "TOTAL" + " " * 31 + "     15.70"
+    assert len(lines[-1]) == len(lines[0])
+
+
+def test_empty_report_has_zero_total():
+    assert expenses.report_lines([]) == [
+        "TOTAL" + " " * 31 + "      0.00"]
+
+
 def test_read_expenses(tmp_path):
     p = tmp_path / "may.csv"
     p.write_text("date,item,amount\n2024-05-03,Tape,3.20\n", encoding="utf-8")
